name: Amoud Foundation
mission: Founded in 1998, the Amoud Foundation impacts the local and global communities by helping people help themselves through sustainable humanitarian projects while maintaining trusting relationships. Amoud is an international humanitarian organization that today serves the people in the Horn of Africa. Amoud also does work on the home-front including helping with the 2006 Hurricane Relief and 2015 Garland Tornado recovery.

strengths_deep_dive: Amoud Foundation maintains high financial efficiency in its delivery of services. In FY2024, the charity allocated a <cite id="5">92.4% program expense ratio</cite> to direct humanitarian programs, outperforming the sector benchmark of 75% and the peer group median of 83.3%. This commitment to low overhead is paired with <cite id="1">12.7 months of working capital held in working capital</cite>, ensuring robust financial security. Furthermore, <cite id="1">Charity Navigator awards the charity an 80/100 overall rating</cite>, highlighting its solid financial health and governance.
rich_narrative.summary: Amoud Foundation provides essential food and education services in Somaliland and Somalia while maintaining high financial efficiency. In FY2024, the charity managed <cite id="5">$11,142,566 in total revenue</cite> to support 15 orphan centers and 2 schools for the deaf and blind. The organization directs its funds toward emergency aid, healthcare programs, and family food packages. Amoud Foundation is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite>, distributing donations directly to poor and needy families (fuqara and masakin). The charity maintains strong financial health, spending a high proportion of its budget on direct charitable services while keeping fundraising costs low. Independent evaluators acknowledge its organizational capacity, as reflected in its <cite id="1">80/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>. Founded in 1998, the foundation has developed nearly three decades of operational history in Horn of Africa crisis zones, although its program scope remains concentrated compared to larger international relief agencies.
